reason: "the person in question, oneself" is a restatement of "the person himself" / 本人. The sentence (手続きは本人が行う) is the plain core use: the individual concerned, not a delegate. Nothing in the sentence needs a gloss the line does not already give.

"under one's arm" is the armpit/side-of-torso sense already carried by currentEN "armpit"; 脇に抱える is that body region used as a carrying spot, not a separate meaning. Worth flagging the reverse of the usual asymmetry here: the Chinese list (旁边/侧面) does NOT carry the 腋下 sense that the evidence translation uses, so ZH lags EN on this entry — but the sense itself is already glossed, so adding it would duplicate.
"loss of employment" is the definition of "unemployment"/失业, and 失業する in the sentence is the ordinary verbal use of the same noun. No referent shift.
"homemaker" is a straight synonym of "housewife"; the "full-time" qualifier is supplied by 専業 in the sentence, not by 主婦. Same sense, different words.
"achieving a desired goal" is the dictionary definition of "success"/成功, restated. 実験が成功した is the core use.
会議中 is the suffixal "in the middle of / in progress" use, which currentEN "during" already names (and ZH 之中 sits alongside it). A learner reading "during" beside 会議中 gets "during a meeting" directly.

"feeling of moral guilt" glosses the sentence's phrase 罪の意識, not 罪 itself — the "feeling" head comes from 意識 (the emotion word is 罪悪感). 罪 in this sentence is still the wrongdoing/sin sense already listed as "sin"/罪过.
"having a unique characteristic" is the adjectival (独特な) surface of the same noun sense "uniqueness"/独特. Grammatical form, not a new meaning.

山田博士 is the honorific-title use attached to a personal name (Dr. Yamada) — the word denotes the person addressed, not the degree. currentEN "doctorate, PhD" names only the qualification, so a learner reading that gloss line beside this sentence gets "Yamada doctorate is famous for plant research" with no cue that 博士 works like a suffixed title (cf. 先生). This is the EN-lags-ZH pattern again: the Chinese list ALREADY carries the sense, because Chinese 博士 is itself both the degree and the form of address (山田博士 reads correctly in the ZH translation), while English needs a separate title gloss. Same shape as the accepted 針 (needle -> clock hand) and 単位 (unit -> credit) gaps: one word, two referents.
"feeling of discontent" restates "dissatisfaction, displeasure"/不满. 不満を持つ is the core collocation of that same sense.

約束を守る falls under the observe/abide-by sense already listed as "to obey" — and ZH 遵守 is the exact verb the evidence translation uses (遵守约定). Both lists cover it; only the English collocation ("keep" vs "obey") differs.
"applying a rule or law" is the prototypical instance of "application"/适用 — 規則が適用される is exactly what the existing gloss denotes, with the rule/law part supplied by the sentence.

An inanimate subject (この道は…に至る) does not create a new sense: dictionaries give the road-reaches-a-place example under the primary 到達 sense, which currentEN "to reach" and currentZH 到达 already state. "leads to" is an English rendering choice.

"enlarging an image or display" is precisely currentEN "magnification" — zooming a screen is that sense applied to a screen. Noting the reverse asymmetry again: currentZH 扩大/扩展 lean toward "broaden in scope" and lack 放大, which the evidence ZH uses, so ZH is the weaker list here — but the sense is already glossed on the card.
"representative or proxy for someone" repeats currentEN "proxy" verbatim in substance; 父の代理で出席 is the core use of 代理/代理.
"outrageous or absurd" is covered by currentEN "ridiculous" and currentZH 岂有此理/出乎意料; とんでもない嘘 is that same evaluative sense.
